scope: Existing small-data CIFAR10/ResNet18, five Non-IID clients, full-network40round FedAvg; adapted attack, same-client P/C. Separate-client FUBA not evaluated here.
established: The tested pre/post weight geometry edits do not provide reliable purification across the four seeds.

Poison records already fit their assigned attacker labels in98.89%-100% of cases before deletion, while new-image trigger ASR is6.06%-8.06%. This shows a training-fit/generalization distinction; it is not a proof of a unique memorization mechanism.
Loss-benefit and input-margin-gradient audits do not identify enough poison records to support source purification.
not_established: A novel mechanism separating normal Non-IID deletion changes from attack release.
Superiority to formal TSBD/RNP/ANP/OTBR or recent null-space defenses.
method_selection_gates: Hold post model, retained information, repair operation and budget fixed; isolate the value of the real pre model against post-only and unrelated-reference controls.
Preserve legitimate post-deletion functions, including minority-client/class behavior; do not count restoring pre as successful repair.
Show an improved safety-utility-data/compute frontier on independent runs; novelty does not follow from before/after comparison, projection, or an extra constraint.
Distinguish any new/private validation information from what is available to baselines.
A learned before-model reference does not automatically preserve certified forgetting.
operational_notes: Initial v2 folded/explicit operations differed by0.0036 logits under reduced precision. The final explicit version disables TF32 and passes the independent wrapper check; the failed run remains separate.
The v4 batch stopped with a nonzero status and empty log on a prior-control fit. Two controls were rerun unchanged in controls_retry_v4 and completed.
All fitting/checkpoint selection preceded test ASR evaluation within each run. Seed71 was repeatedly used for development; it is not an independent test.
Inference rounding can change a few predictions relative to earlier TF32-enabled reports; all current comparisons use the same explicit arithmetic policy.
